newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels issue statement with released hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels issue statement with released hostages.

text.p: The following is a translation of the seven-point statement issued by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas with the first hostages released Sunday night.

1. The MRTA was born in the country to struggle for the problems that marginalize the large majority of Peruvians, especially in the period of the government of President Alberto Fujimori that also worsened and increased poverty dramatically in Peru ... (text not heard) ... and to seek the liberty of our comrades.
2. We make this proposal. So that the people see that we want to find a solution peacefully and respectful of the feeling of our people, we are prepared to release hostages.
3. However, Fujimori's message on the day of December 21 put into practice an unhelpful attitude while we look for true peace.

4. Despite this, and showing an attitude different to the government, which uses unacceptable terms (and) only worsens the sitution by cutting off the basic services that made the hostages' situation harder, we proceed to liberate people who are not directly or indirectly linked to the policy of the regime as a Christmas gesture.

5. The people linked to the regime -- minister, vice ministers, members of the judiciary and legislators, leaders of the armed and police forces, and representatives of the Japanese businesses -- will remain.
6. In the same way, the diplomats from Asia and Latin America, whose exits we will be evaluating.

7. We clarify and ratify that the freedom of the authorities that today remain prisoners will only be possible if the government frees the comrades. If Mr. Fujimori decides on a military solution, he will always find a Tupac Amaru member ready to remain vigilant in the defence of the interests of the people, defending our rights to work and the right to life of our brothers in the struggle."
